title: Deterministic schema class dispatch performance scenario
description: The ordered workload proves the authored semantic outcome and performance declaration.

parameters.scenario: exercise Class 1 through Class 4, Class 3 with no affected scope, unsupported reset, and push/pull/rebuild mismatch
parameters.defect: emit fetch, omit replace or rebuild, destroy queue, continue partial work, or accept a non-current manifest

steps.description: Observe exact-current schema dispatch for an independent client.
Repeat exact-current schema dispatch for another client.
Repeat exact-current schema dispatch for a third client.
Establish baseline scope membership for the first Class 1 client.
Establish baseline scope membership for the second Class 1 client.
Establish baseline scope membership for the third Class 1 client.
Materialize an empty transaction before the Class 1 membership generation.
Advance the durable materialization boundary for the Class 1 generation.
Stage a server-only membership generation without a schema manifest change.
Activate the server-only membership generation for scope A.
Observe Class 1 membership dispatch after its active generation changes.
Repeat Class 1 membership dispatch for another affected client.
Repeat Class 1 membership dispatch for a third affected client.
Start and warm the first Class 2 client at schema version 1.
Start and warm the second Class 2 client at schema version 1.
Start and warm the third Class 2 client at schema version 1.
Publish an additive nullable field as a compatible Class 2 manifest.
Observe compatible Class 2 schema replacement.
Repeat compatible Class 2 schema replacement.
Repeat compatible Class 2 schema replacement for a third client.
Start and warm the first affected Class 3 client at schema version 2.
Start and warm the second affected Class 3 client at schema version 2.
Start and warm the third affected Class 3 client at schema version 2.
Start and warm the first unaffected Class 3 client at schema version 2.
Start and warm the second unaffected Class 3 client at schema version 2.
Start and warm the third unaffected Class 3 client at schema version 2.
Start and warm the first Class 4 client at schema version 2.
Start and warm the second Class 4 client at schema version 2.
Start and warm the third Class 4 client at schema version 2.
Publish a historical materialization field as a Class 3 manifest for scope A.
Observe Class 3 rebuild dispatch for an affected assigned scope.
Repeat Class 3 rebuild dispatch for another affected client.
Repeat Class 3 rebuild dispatch for a third affected client.
Observe Class 3 replacement when no assigned scope is affected.
Repeat unaffected Class 3 replacement for another client.
Repeat unaffected Class 3 replacement for a third client.
Start and warm the first Class 4 client at schema version 3.
Start and warm the second Class 4 client at schema version 3.
Start and warm the third Class 4 client at schema version 3.
Publish an incompatible value-type change as a Class 4 manifest.
Observe Class 4 unsupported dispatch.
Repeat Class 4 unsupported dispatch for another client.
Repeat Class 4 unsupported dispatch for a third client.

assertions.description: The ordered workload produces the complete authored durable semantic outcome without partial state.
Each bound sample records the required schema dispatch from its executed connect operation.
Every declared budget or measurement records all configured strata and required metrics.
